place: A stencil yard of lifted frisket plates, each a hard-edged masked sheet at its own height, dusted by one soft spray that grades from peach to cyan across the whole island.

observations.what: Hard crisp contour of the upper lid fold where a frisket mask was lifted
Atomized pale buff mist across the sclera with no bristle track
Spray fading from warm peach at the left lid to cold cyan and black at the right
Gouache spatter specks over the black on the right

measured.role: Deep outer space void, central pupil, and deepest eyelid crease shadows
Soft shadow framing the eyeball and shading the socket
Dark teal-grey transitional tones between space and the eyelid rim
Midtone skin shading along the brow ridge and eyelid margins
Outer ring of the iris and shadowed face of the planetary ring
Pale highlight tone across the sclera and inner lower lid margin
Desaturated beige midtone bridging lid highlights to shadow
Warm brown-red vascular shading in the medial caruncle and crease

palette.notes: Four flat steps of one spray: peach sand, rose dirt, lilac stone and cyan grass, each clean and bright; the board shows through as a warm cream void.

A flat decal of gouache spatter: white and cyan dots of three sizes scattered over the cell.

creatures.name: stencil-eye
creatures.source: The eye as the painter built it: sclera, iris and pupil each sprayed through its own cut mask.

shape.summary: Three upright stencil plates stacked front to back: a peach almond sclera sheet, a blue iris ring sheet with a lime zigzag cut, and a black pupil disc, on a masking-tape plinth with overspray blocks at the edges.

creatures.pose: stencil stack: the eye as three cut frisket plates standing upright one in front of another, sclera at the back, iris ring in the middle, pupil disc at the front, facing the camera.
creatures.why: ANALYSIS.medium.technique names frisket stencils; the eye becomes the stack of masks that made it.

composition.mass: The plates step down from the back row toward the camera.
composition.read: A studio floor of cut masks with the eye standing as the mask stack that made it.

lighting.notes: The board surface is hidden under opaque paint lit evenly for the artist (ANALYSIS.medium.surface); a pale board void reads as the studio around the stencil.

rules: Plates keep one surface each; no cobble inside a plate.
Stencil sheets stand on plate corners, never on the path.

lens.aspect: ANALYSIS.medium.technique and edges: frisket stencils give hard crisp contours, the airbrush gives atomized fog that never shows a stroke
lens.place: A stencil yard of lifted frisket plates, each a hard-edged masked sheet at its own height, dusted by one soft spray that grades from peach to cyan across the whole island.
lens.summary: Flat stencil plates at three heights, each plate one clean colour step of a single spray gradient, with masking-tape rolls, cut stencil sheets and overspray plumes standing on them.
lens.differs: Round-4 medium read the airbrush as soft radial terraces around the pupil; here the hard frisket edge is the terrain and the gradient runs straight across rectangular plates, with no rings and no pupil column.

shaper.name: patchwork
shaper.why: Frisket masks are cut sheets laid edge to edge; each becomes a flat rectangular plate at its own height with a hard cliff where the mask lifted (ANALYSIS.medium.edges).

surface_mix.why: Each mask holds one flat colour; the finish orders the plates so one spray pass crosses them in four clean steps, warm left to cold right, as the painting's temperature split runs (ANALYSIS.palette.temperature).

cliff_treatment.why: A lifted mask leaves a clean vertical edge; sheer cliffs with no bands keep every plate reading as a cut sheet.

lighting.time: flat spray-booth daylight over a drawing board
lighting.why: The board surface is hidden under opaque paint lit evenly for the artist (ANALYSIS.medium.surface); a pale board void reads as the studio around the stencil.
